    Signals are signed integers: +v means variable v is true, -v means
    variable v is false.  Gate outputs are always fresh variables.

        self.clauses: list[list[int]] = []

        return self.num_vars

        self.clauses.append([v] if value else [-v])
        return v

        self.clauses.append([-z, b])
        self.clauses.append([z, -a, -b])
        return z

        z = self._new()
        # z <-> (a or b)
        self.clauses.append([z, -a])
        self.clauses.append([z, -b])
        self.clauses.append([-z, a, b])

        self.clauses.append([a, b, -z])
        self.clauses.append([a, -b, z])
        self.clauses.append([-a, b, z])

        bc = circuit.and_(b, carry)

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to SAT.

Instance of Subset Sum: {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
Instance of SAT: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}

The reduction builds a Boolean circuit that computes the sum of the
selected numbers and asserts it equals the target.  The circuit is a
chain of ripple-carry adders, one per input number; each number a_i is
gated by a fresh selection variable x_i.  The circuit is then converted
to CNF with the standard Tseitin transformation (each gate gets a fresh
variable and clauses defining it).  The size is polynomial in the input
size (number of numbers times the bit length of the target), so the
reduction runs in polynomial time.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


class _Circuit:
    """A small Boolean circuit builder with Tseitin CNF output.

    Signals are signed integers: +v means variable v is true, -v means
    variable v is false.  Gate outputs are always fresh variables.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.num_vars = 0
        self.clauses: list[list[int]] = []

    def _new(self) -> int:
        self.num_vars += 1
        return self.num_vars

    def constant(self, value: bool) -> int:
        v = self._new()
        self.clauses.append([v] if value else [-v])
        return v

    def and_(self, a: int, b: int) -> int:
        z = self._new()
        # z <-> (a and b)
        self.clauses.append([-z, a])
        self.clauses.append([-z, b])
        self.clauses.append([z, -a, -b])
        return z

    def or_(self, a: int, b: int) -> int:
        z = self._new()
        # z <-> (a or b)
        self.clauses.append([z, -a])
        self.clauses.append([z, -b])
        self.clauses.append([-z, a, b])
        return z

    def xor(self, a: int, b: int) -> int:
        z = self._new()
        # z <-> (a xor b)
        self.clauses.append([-a, -b, -z])
        self.clauses.append([a, b, -z])
        self.clauses.append([a, -b, z])
        self.clauses.append([-a, b, z])
        return z

    def unit(self, lit: int, value: bool) -> None:
        self.clauses.append([lit] if value else [-lit])

    def force_false(self) -> None:
        # An unsatisfiable clause.
        self.clauses.append([])


def _add(circuit, a_bits, b_bits, false_lit):
    """Ripple-carry addition of two little-endian bit lists."""
    n = max(len(a_bits), len(b_bits))
    result = []
    carry = false_lit
    for j in range(n):
        a = a_bits[j] if j < len(a_bits) else false_lit
        b = b_bits[j] if j < len(b_bits) else false_lit
        s = circuit.xor(circuit.xor(a, b), carry)
        ab = circuit.and_(a, b)
        ac = circuit.and_(a, carry)
        bc = circuit.and_(b, carry)
        carry = circuit.or_(circuit.or_(ab, ac), bc)
        result.append(s)
    result.append(carry)
    return result


def reduce(instance):
    numbers = instance["numbers"]
    target = instance["target"]

    # t < 0 is always no: emit an unsatisfiable formula.
    if target < 0:
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": [[]]}

    # t = 0 is always yes: the empty sub-list works.
    if target == 0:
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": []}

    # Any number larger than the (non-negative) target can never be used,
    # because all numbers are non-negative.
    usable = [a for a in numbers if a <= target]

    circuit = _Circuit()
    false_lit = circuit.constant(False)

    # acc holds the little-endian bits of the running sum.
    acc = [false_lit]
    for a in usable:
        x = circuit._new()  # selection variable for this number
        # partial product bits: x AND bit_j(a)
        pp = []
        value = a
        while value:
            pp.append(x if (value & 1) else false_lit)
            value >>= 1
        if not pp:
            pp = [false_lit]
        acc = _add(circuit, acc, pp, false_lit)

    # Assert acc == target, bit by bit (little-endian).
    target_bits = []
    value = target
    while value:
        target_bits.append(value & 1)
        value >>= 1
    if not target_bits:
        target_bits = [0]

    width = max(len(acc), len(target_bits))
    for j in range(width):
        desired = target_bits[j] if j < len(target_bits) else 0
        if j < len(acc):
            circuit.unit(acc[j], desired == 1)
        elif desired == 1:
            # A target bit that the sum cannot produce: unsatisfiable.
            circuit.force_false()

    return {"num_vars": circuit.num_vars, "clauses": circuit.clauses}

SOURCE (Subset Sum): {"numbers": [a1, a2, ...], "target": t}
    numbers are non-negative ints (may repeat); t is any int.
    Yes iff some sub-list sums to exactly t.

TARGET (SAT): {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}
    Variables 1..m; literal +v / -v.  Yes iff some assignment satisfies
    every clause.

Construction
------------
For each number a_i we introduce a selection variable x_i (x_i true means
a_i is taken).  We then build a ripple-carry binary adder circuit, in CNF
via a Tseitin encoding, that computes

        acc = sum_i (x_i * a_i)

one number at a time.  The accumulator starts at 0 and has B bits, where
B = (sum of all numbers).bit_length(); every reachable sum is < 2^B, so B
bits suffice.  Finally we assert acc == target bit by bit.

The circuit is deterministic in the x_i, so the formula is satisfiable iff
some choice of numbers sums to target.

Trivial cases:
    t < 0                  -> unsatisfiable formula
    t = 0                  -> satisfiable formula (empty sub-list)
    t > sum(numbers)       -> unsatisfiable formula

The construction uses O(n * B) variables and clauses, i.e. polynomial in
the encoding length of the instance.  No brute-force solver is invoked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def reduce(instance):
    numbers = instance["numbers"]
    target = instance["target"]

    # --- Trivial cases -------------------------------------------------
    if target < 0:
        # No sub-list can sum to a negative target.
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": [[]]}  # unsatisfiable

    if target == 0:
        # The empty sub-list always sums to 0.
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": []}  # satisfiable

    total = sum(numbers)
    if target > total:
        # Every sub-list sums to at most total.
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": [[]]}  # unsatisfiable

    # --- Tseitin circuit builder --------------------------------------
    num_vars = 0
    clauses = []

    def new_var():
        nonlocal num_vars
        num_vars += 1
        return num_vars

    def add_clause(*literals):
        clauses.append(list(literals))

    # A variable forced to false, used for constant 0 bits.
    false_var = new_var()
    add_clause(-false_var)

    def xor2(a, b):
        """New variable equal to a XOR b."""
        out = new_var()
        add_clause(a, b, -out)
        add_clause(a, -b, out)
        add_clause(-a, b, out)
        add_clause(-a, -b, -out)
        return out

    def and2(a, b):
        """New variable equal to a AND b."""
        out = new_var()
        add_clause(-a, -b, out)
        add_clause(a, -out)
        add_clause(b, -out)
        return out

    def or2(a, b):
        """New variable equal to a OR b."""
        out = new_var()
        add_clause(a, b, -out)
        add_clause(-a, out)
        add_clause(-b, out)
        return out

    def full_adder(p, q, r):
        """Return (sum, carry) for the one-bit sum p + q + r."""
        t = xor2(p, q)
        s = xor2(t, r)
        u1 = and2(p, q)
        u2 = and2(p, r)
        u3 = and2(q, r)
        v = or2(u1, u2)
        c = or2(v, u3)
        return s, c

    # B bits are enough to hold every reachable sum (all < 2^B).
    B = total.bit_length()

    # Selection variable per number.
    select = [new_var() for _ in numbers]

    # Accumulator, initially zero.
    acc = [false_var] * B

    for i, a in enumerate(numbers):
        carry = false_var
        new_acc = []
        for j in range(B):
            p = acc[j]
            q = select[i] if (a >> j) & 1 else false_var
            s, carry = full_adder(p, q, carry)
            new_acc.append(s)
        # The final carry out of the top bit is always 0 because the sum is
        # at most `total` < 2^B; assert it for safety.
        add_clause(-carry)
        acc = new_acc

    # Assert accumulator == target, bit by bit.
    for j in range(B):
        if (target >> j) & 1:
            add_clause(acc[j])
        else:
            add_clause(-acc[j])

    return {"num_vars": num_vars, "clauses": clauses}

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to SAT."""

from __future__ import annotations


def reduce(instance):
    numbers = instance["numbers"]
    target = instance["target"]

    # Trivial cases.
    if target < 0:
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": [[]]}   # unsatisfiable
    if target == 0:
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": []}     # satisfiable

    total = sum(numbers)
    if target > total:
        return {"num_vars": 0, "clauses": [[]]}

    # We build a ripple-carry adder circuit in CNF (Tseitin encoding).
    num_vars = 0
    clauses = []

    def new_var():
        nonlocal num_vars
        num_vars += 1
        return num_vars

    def add_clause(*lits):
        clauses.append(list(lits))

    # Constant variables.
    true_var = new_var()
    add_clause(true_var)
    false_var = new_var()
    add_clause(-false_var)

    def xor2(a, b):
        out = new_var()
        add_clause(a, b, -out)
        add_clause(a, -b, out)
        add_clause(-a, b, out)
        add_clause(-a, -b, -out)
        return out

    def and2(a, b):
        out = new_var()
        add_clause(-a, -b, out)
        add_clause(a, -out)
        add_clause(b, -out)
        return out

    def or2(a, b):
        out = new_var()
        add_clause(a, b, -out)
        add_clause(-a, out)
        add_clause(-b, out)
        return out

    def full_adder(p, q, r):
        t = xor2(p, q)
        s = xor2(t, r)
        u1 = and2(p, q)
        u2 = and2(p, r)
        u3 = and2(q, r)
        v = or2(u1, u2)
        c = or2(v, u3)
        return s, c

    B = total.bit_length()  # 2^(B-1) <= total < 2^B

    # Selection variables for each number.
    select = [new_var() for _ in numbers]

    # Accumulator starts at zero.
    acc = [false_var] * B

    for i, a in enumerate(numbers):
        carry = false_var
        new_acc = []
        for j in range(B):
            p = acc[j]
            q = select[i] if (a >> j) & 1 else false_var
            s, carry = full_adder(p, q, carry)
            new_acc.append(s)
        # carry out of the top bit must be 0 (sum <= total < 2^B)
        add_clause(-carry)
        acc = new_acc

    # Assert accumulator == target.
    for j in range(B):
        bit = (target >> j) & 1
        if bit:
            add_clause(acc[j])
        else:
            add_clause(-acc[j])

    return {"num_vars": num_vars, "clauses": clauses}
